# Save all intermediate results
```{r}
malig <- subset(merge, final.clones == "malig")

df <- as.data.frame.matrix(table(malig$orig.ident, malig$final.clones))
df.ss <- subset(df, malig > 100)
keep <- rownames(df.ss)
malig <- subset(malig, orig.ident %in% keep)
malig.ss <- R2easyviz::r2sample_seurat(malig, n = 1000, barcode_column = "barcode")
split.malig <- SplitObject(malig.ss, split.by = "orig.ident")

split.malig.ss <- split.malig[1:15]

w.combine <- list()

for (sample_name in names(split.malig)) {
  cat("Processing", sample_name, "\n")
  s <- split.malig[[sample_name]]

  # Use log-normalized (non-negative) expression
  mat <- GetAssayData(s, assay = "SCT", slot = "data")

  # Filter genes with very low expression
  mat <- mat[rowSums(mat) > (ncol(mat) / 50), ]
  
  row_var <- rowVars(mat)
  keep <- names(row_var[row_var>.05])
  mat <- as.matrix(mat[keep,])

  # Optional: clip extreme values for stability
  mat[mat > 3] <- 3
  mat[mat < 0] <- 0
  
  for (i in 6:12) {
    out.iter <- NNLM::nnmf(mat, k = i, method = "scd", max.iter = 200, alpha = c(0.01, 0.01, 0.01))
    w.iter <- as.data.frame(out.iter$W)
    colnames(w.iter) <- paste0(sample_name, "_k", i, "_p", seq_len(ncol(w.iter)))

    # Save as a list for flexibility (different gene sets per sample)
    w.combine[[paste0(sample_name, "_k", i)]] <- w.iter
  }
}

saveRDS(w.combine, "~/hpchome/ctcl4.4/int_results/w.combine.rds")

w.combine <- readRDS("~/hpchome/ctcl4.4/int_results/w.combine.rds")
# Step 1: Convert each matrix to a data.frame with gene names as a column
w.dfs <- lapply(w.combine, function(mat) {
  df <- as.data.frame(mat)
  df$gene <- rownames(mat)
  df
})

# Step 2: Full join all data.frames by 'gene', filling missing values with 0
w.merged <- reduce(w.dfs, full_join, by = "gene")

# Step 3: Set gene names as rownames and remove the column
rownames(w.merged) <- w.merged$gene
w.merged$gene <- NULL

# Step 4: Replace NAs with 0
w.mat <- as.matrix(w.merged)
w.mat[is.na(w.mat)] <- 0

# Step 5: Correlation of program columns
#w.mat[w.mat == 0] <- NA
#w.mat <- w.mat[, colSums(w.mat != 0) > 0]
cor.mat <- cor(w.mat)
hist(rowSums(abs(cor.mat)))

rand <- sample(x = 1:ncol(cor.mat), size = 1000, replace = F)
pheatmap(cor.mat[rand,rand], show_colnames = F, show_rownames = F)

cor.mat.ss <- cor.mat[rowSums(cor.mat >.7) >10 , rowSums(cor.mat >.7) >20]
pheatmap(cor.mat.ss, show_colnames = F, show_rownames = F)



pheatmap(cor.mat, show_colnames = F, show_rownames = F)
orig.ident <- sapply(str_split(string = colnames(cor.mat), pattern = "_", n = 2), `[`, 1)
annotation_col <- data.frame(orig.ident = orig.ident)
rownames(annotation_col) <- colnames(cor.mat)

pheatmap(cor.mat, show_colnames = F, show_rownames = F, annotation_col = annotation_col)

# cor_mat: your correlation matrix (e.g., Pearson or cosine)

  # Hierarchical clustering (you can replace this with k-means if appropriate)

})
```

# Try 2 -- Save only stable MPs per sample
```{r}
w.combine <- readRDS("~/hpchome/ctcl4.4/int_results/w.combine.rds")

samples <- sapply(str_split(string = names(w.combine), pattern = "_", n = 2), `[`, 1)
samples <- unique(samples)


by_sample <- lapply(samples, function(samp) {
  # Match names that start with the sample followed by "_" (e.g., "S1_")
  matched_names <- grep(paste0("^", samp, "_"), names(w.combine), value = TRUE)
  
  # Subset the data frames by name
  matching_dfs <- w.combine[matched_names]
  
  # Column-bind all matched data frames
  do.call(cbind, matching_dfs)
})

# Assign sample names to the result
names(by_sample) <- samples

sample_metaprograms <- list()
samples.ss <- samples[1:5]  # Assuming this is a character vector of names
k.range <- 4:16             # Define k.range
penalty_weight <- 0.02

for (s in seq_along(samples)) {
  sample_name <- samples[s]
  mat <- as.matrix(by_sample[[sample_name]])
  
  # Step 1: Correlation and filtering
  cor_mat <- cor(mat, method = "pearson")
  keep <- rowSums(cor_mat > 0.85) > 2
  cor_ss <- cor_mat[keep, keep]
  
  # Step 2: Distance + clustering
  dist_mat <- as.dist(1 - cor_ss)
  hc <- hclust(dist_mat, method = "ward.D2")
  
  sil_width <- numeric(length(k.range))
  names(sil_width) <- k.range
  clustering_results <- list()
  
  for (j in seq_along(k.range)) {
    k <- k.range[j]
    clusters <- cutree(hc, k)
    
    if (length(unique(clusters)) > 1) {
      sil <- silhouette(clusters, dist_mat)
      sil_width[j] <- mean(sil[, 3])
      clustering_results[[as.character(k)]] <- clusters
    } else {
      sil_width[j] <- NA
    }
  }
  
  # Step 3: Penalized score and best k
  penalized_score <- sil_width - penalty_weight * k.range
  best_k <- k.range[which.max(penalized_score)]
  final_clusters <- as.data.frame(clustering_results[[as.character(best_k)]])
  colnames(final_clusters) <- "Clusters"
  # Step 4: Collapse gene expression by cluster
  mat <- mat[, colnames(mat) %in% colnames(cor_ss)]
  mat_df <- as.data.frame(t(mat))
  mat_df$cluster <- final_clusters$Clusters
  
  gene_sums <- mat_df %>%
    group_by(cluster) %>%
    summarise(across(where(is.numeric), sum, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  
  gene_sums <- as.matrix(gene_sums[,-1])
  
  rownames(gene_sums) <- paste0(sample_name, "_", "MetaProgram", "_", 1:nrow(gene_sums))  # exclude cluster column

  gene_sums_df <- as.data.frame(t(gene_sums))
  
  sample_metaprograms[[sample_name]] <- gene_sums_df
  
  print(paste0("Finished_", sample_name))
}

################################### Merge Metaprograms ##############################################
```

```{r}
dist_mat.all <- as.dist(as.matrix(1 - cor.w.mat))  # Higher correlation → smaller distance

cosine_sim <- function(x, y) {
  valid <- which(!is.na(x) & !is.na(y))
  if (length(valid) < 5) return(NA)
  sum(x[valid] * y[valid]) / (sqrt(sum(x[valid]^2)) * sqrt(sum(y[valid]^2)))
}

cosine_sim_matrix <- function(mat) {
  n <- ncol(mat)
  sim_mat <- matrix(NA, n, n)
  colnames(sim_mat) <- colnames(mat)
  rownames(sim_mat) <- colnames(mat)
  
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    for (j in i:n) {
      x <- mat[, i]
      y <- mat[, j]
      val <- cosine_sim(x, y)
      sim_mat[i, j] <- val
      sim_mat[j, i] <- val
    }
  }
  return(sim_mat)
}
```

```{r}
library(lsa)  # cosine()
cosine_sim_matrix <- function(mat) {
  mat <- as.matrix(mat)

  # Remove columns with all NAs or zero magnitude
  keep <- colSums(!is.na(mat)) > 1 & colSums(abs(mat), na.rm = TRUE) > 0
  mat <- mat[, keep, drop = FALSE]

  # Number of metaprograms
  n <- ncol(mat)
  cos.sim <- matrix(NA, n, n)
  colnames(cos.sim) <- colnames(mat)
  rownames(cos.sim) <- colnames(mat)

  for (i in 1:n) {
    for (j in i:n) {
      x <- mat[, i]
      y <- mat[, j]
      idx <- which(!is.na(x) & !is.na(y))
      if (length(idx) > 1) {
        sim <- sum(x[idx] * y[idx]) / (sqrt(sum(x[idx]^2)) * sqrt(sum(y[idx]^2)))
        cos.sim[i, j] <- sim
        cos.sim[j, i] <- sim
      }
    }
  }

  return(cos.sim)
}
```

```{r}
library(GeneNMF)
tcr_genes <- grep("^TR[ABDG][VDJC]", rownames(merge), value = TRUE)
ig_genes <- grep("^IG[JHKL][VDJCMG]", rownames(merge), value = TRUE)

malig.ss <- subset(merge, final.clones == "malig" & orig.ident %in% sample(unique(merge$orig.ident), 5))

split.malig <- SplitObject(malig.ss, split.by = "orig.ident")

split.malig <- lapply(split.malig, function(x) {
  x <- FindVariableFeatures(x, nfeatures = 10000)
  VariableFeatures(x) <- setdiff(VariableFeatures(x), c(tcr_genes,ig_genes))
  return(x)
})

vf.list <- lapply(split.malig, VariableFeatures)

geneNMF.programs <- multiNMF(split.malig, assay="SCT", slot="data", k=c(4:8), min.exp = 0.05, center = T, scale = T)
geneNMF.metaprograms <- getMetaPrograms(geneNMF.programs,
                                        metric = "cosine",
                                        weight.explained = 0.8,
                                        nMP=12, max.genes = 100, min.confidence = 0.6)

GeneNMF::plotMetaPrograms(geneNMF.metaprograms)
```


```{r}

#TRY 2
malig <- subset(merge, cloneType == "Hyperexpanded (0.1 < X <= 1)" & final.clones == "malig")

df <- as.data.frame.matrix(table(malig$orig.ident, malig$final.clones))
df.ss <- subset(df, malig > 100)
keep <- rownames(df.ss)
malig <- subset(malig, orig.ident %in% keep)
malig.ss <- R2easyviz::r2sample_seurat(malig, n = 1000, barcode_column = "barcode")
split.malig <- SplitObject(malig.ss, split.by = "orig.ident")

top50_list <- list()
split.malig.ss <- split.malig[1:25]

w.combine <- list()  # Collect all W matrices in a list instead of cbind

for (sample_name in names(split.malig.ss)) {
  cat("Processing", sample_name, "\n")
  s <- split.malig.ss[[sample_name]]

  # Use log-normalized (non-negative) expression
  mat <- GetAssayData(s, assay = "SCT", slot = "data")

  # Filter genes with very low expression
  mat <- mat[rowSums(mat) > (ncol(mat) / 50), ]
  
  row_var <- rowVars(mat)
  keep <- names(row_var[row_var>.05])
  mat <- as.matrix(mat[keep,])

  # Optional: clip extreme values for stability
  mat[mat > 3] <- 3
  mat[mat < 0] <- 0
  
  for (i in 6:12) {
    out.iter <- NNLM::nnmf(mat, k = i, method = "scd", max.iter = 200, alpha = c(0, 0.01, .01))
    w.iter <- as.data.frame(out.iter$W)
    colnames(w.iter) <- paste0(sample_name, "_k", i, "_p", seq_len(ncol(w.iter)))

    # Save as a list for flexibility (different gene sets per sample)
    w.combine[[paste0(sample_name, "_k", i)]] <- w.iter
  }
}

w.mat[is.na(w.mat)] <- 0
```

```{r}
malig <- subset(merge, cloneType == "Hyperexpanded (0.1 < X <= 1)" & final.clones == "malig")

df <- as.data.frame.matrix(table(malig$orig.ident, malig$final.clones))
df.ss <- subset(df, malig > 100)
keep <- rownames(df.ss)
malig <- subset(malig, orig.ident %in% keep)
malig.ss <- R2easyviz::r2sample_seurat(malig, n = 1000, barcode_column = "barcode")
split.malig <- SplitObject(malig.ss, split.by = "orig.ident")

top50_list <- list()
split.malig.ss <- split.malig[1:15]

for (sample_name in names(split.malig.ss)) {
  cat("Processing", sample_name, "\n")
  s <- split.malig[[sample_name]]

  mat <- s@assays$SCT@data
  hist(rowSums(mat), breaks = 5000, xlim = c(0,50))
  mat <- mat[rowSums(mat) > (ncol(mat)/100),]
  mat <- as.matrix(mat)

  mat.scale <- scale(t(mat), center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
  mat.scale <- t(mat.scale)
  mat.scale[mat.scale > 3] <- 3
  mat.scale[mat.scale < 0] <- 0

  for (i in 6:12) {
    out.iter <- NNLM::nnmf(mat.scale, k = i, method = "scd", max.iter = 200, alpha = c(0,0,0))
    w.iter <- as.data.frame(out.iter[["W"]])
    if (i == 6) {
      w.combine <- w.iter
    } else {
      w.combine <- cbind(w.combine, w.iter)
    }
  }

  cor.w.combine <- cor(w.combine)

  colnames(cor.w.combine) <- paste0("W", 1:ncol(cor.w.combine))
  colnames(w.combine) <- paste0("W", 1:ncol(w.combine))

  keep_idx <- rowSums(cor.w.combine > 0.8) > 2
  cor.w.combine <- cor.w.combine[keep_idx, keep_idx]

  dist_mat <- as.dist(1 - cor.w.combine)

  k.range <- 2:20
  sil_width <- numeric(length(k.range))
  clustering_results <- list()

  for (j in seq_along(k.range)) {
    k <- k.range[j]
    hc <- hclust(dist_mat, method = "ward.D2")
    cluster_assignments <- cutree(hc, k = k)
    sil <- silhouette(cluster_assignments, dist_mat)
    sil_width[j] <- mean(sil[, 3])
    clustering_results[[as.character(k)]] <- cluster_assignments
  }


  best_k <- k.range[which.max(sil_width)]
  clusters <- cutree(hclust(dist_mat, method = "ward.D2"), k = best_k)

  cor.w.combine.df <- as.data.frame(cor.w.combine)
  cor.w.combine.df$clusters <- clusters

  keep <- colnames(cor.w.combine)
  w.combine <- w.combine[, keep, drop = FALSE]
  test <- t(w.combine)
  test <- as.data.frame(test)
  test$cluster <- clusters

  df_sums <- test %>%
    group_by(cluster) %>%
    summarise(across(where(is.numeric), sum, na.rm = TRUE))
  df_sums <- t(df_sums)
  df_sums <- df_sums[-1, , drop = FALSE]
  colnames(df_sums) <- paste0("Cluster", 1:ncol(df_sums))
  df_sums <- as.data.frame(df_sums)

  top50_rownames <- apply(df_sums, 2, function(col) {
    names(sort(col, decreasing = TRUE))[1:50]
  })

  top50_list[[sample_name]] <- top50_rownames
}
```

```{r}
k_values <- 6:12
# Apply NMF to each matrix in scale_data_list for each k in k_values
nmf_result.list <- lapply(scale_data_list.pos, function(scale_data) {
  result <- lapply(k_values, function(k) {
    out <- NNLM::nnmf(scale_data, k = k, method = "lee", max.iter = 100, alpha = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.01))
    return(out)
  })
  # Name the inner list with k_values
  names(result) <- paste0("k", k_values)
  return(result)
})

saveRDS(nmf_result.list, "nmf_result.list.rds")

w_matrices_by_sample <- lapply(nmf_result.list, function(sample_results) {
  # For each sample, extract the W matrix for each k value
  w_list <- lapply(sample_results, function(result) {
    result$W
  })
  # Combine (cbind) all the W matrices for the sample into a single matrix
  merged_w <- do.call(cbind, w_list)
  return(merged_w)
})

# List to store final top 50 gene lists (MPs) for each sample/cluster combination
top50_all_samples <- list()

# Iterate over each sample (names from w_matrices_by_sample, assumed to be created previously)
for(sample_name in names(w_matrices_by_sample)) {
  sample_w <- w_matrices_by_sample[[sample_name]]
  colnames(sample_w) <- paste0("W", 1:ncol(sample_w))

  # Compute the correlation matrix between columns (factors)
  cor_w <- cor(sample_w, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  # Set the diagonal to NA so that self-correlations are ignored
  diag(cor_w) <- NA
  # For each column, get the maximum correlation with any other column
  num_correlated <- apply(cor_w, 2, function(x) sum(x > 0.85, na.rm = TRUE))

  # Keep only those columns with at least 3 other columns correlated above 0.8
  keep_cols <- names(num_correlated)[num_correlated >= 3]
  
  if(length(keep_cols) < 2) {
    message("Sample ", sample_name, " has fewer than 2 correlated columns after filtering; skipping.")
    next
  }
  # Retain only those columns (factors) that meet the threshold
  sample_w <- sample_w[, keep_cols, drop = FALSE]
  
  # ---- End new filtering step ----
  
  # Define range of k values to test
  k_values <- 6:12
  
  # Run cluster_summary on sample_w directly (not on its correlation matrix)
  summary_stats <- cluster_summary(sample_w, k_values)
  
  # Pick the best k: the one with the highest silhouette value
  best_k <- summary_stats$k[which.max(summary_stats$silhouette)]
  
  message("For sample ", sample_name, " best k (centers) = ", best_k)
  
  # Run k-means clustering on the transposed sample_w matrix (so that factors become observations)
  set.seed(123)  # for reproducibility
  sample_w_clus <- kmeans(t(sample_w), centers = best_k, nstart = 15, iter.max = 25)
  
  # Combine the clustering assignments with the transposed matrix
  mat_with_clusters <- cbind(t(sample_w), cluster = sample_w_clus$cluster)
  mat_with_clusters <- as.data.frame(mat_with_clusters)
  
  # Extract top 50 genes per cluster for this sample using your helper function
  sample_top50 <- lapply(1:best_k, function(cluster_id) {
    get_top_50_per_cluster(mat_with_clusters, cluster_id)
  })
  # Name each element with sample and cluster info
  names(sample_top50) <- paste0(sample_name, "_Cluster_", 1:best_k)
  
  # Save into our overall list
  top50_all_samples[[sample_name]] <- sample_top50
}

# Merge all top50 lists from all samples into one list (flatten one level)
all_top50 <- unlist(top50_all_samples, recursive = FALSE)


# ---------------------------
# Now compute an overlap matrix among all MPs (top 50 lists)

n_mps <- length(all_top50)
overlap_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = n_mps, ncol = n_mps)
mp_names <- names(all_top50)
rownames(overlap_matrix) <- mp_names
colnames(overlap_matrix) <- mp_names

# Calculate pairwise overlaps (number of shared genes)
for(i in 1:n_mps){
  for(j in 1:n_mps){
    overlap_matrix[i, j] <- length(intersect(all_top50[[i]], all_top50[[j]]))
  }
}

# Plot the overlap matrix as a heatmap
heatmap_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("white", "red"))(100)

# Plot the heatmap
pheatmap(overlap_matrix, 
         cluster_rows = TRUE, 
         cluster_cols = TRUE, 
         display_numbers = FALSE, 
         main = "Overlap of Top 50 Genes (MPs) Across Samples", 
         color = heatmap_colors)

         cluster_rows = TRUE,
```

```{r}
k_values <- 2:50

# Initialize a vector to store average silhouette scores
avg_silhouette_scores <- numeric(length(k_values))

# Loop over each k and compute the average silhouette score
for (k in k_values) {
  # Perform k-means clustering
  kmeans_result <- kmeans(overlap_matrix, centers = k, nstart = 25)
  
  # Compute silhouette information
  silhouette_info <- silhouette(kmeans_result$cluster, dist(overlap_matrix))
  
  # Store the average silhouette score
  avg_silhouette_scores[k - 1] <- mean(silhouette_info[, 3])
}

plot(k_values, avg_silhouette_scores, type = "b", pch = 19,
```

```{r}
# Function to extract the top 50 gene names (columns) per cluster based on summed expression values
get_top_50_per_cluster <- function(mat_with_clusters, cluster_id) {
  # Subset rows (cells) belonging to the specified cluster
  cluster_data <- mat_with_clusters[mat_with_clusters$cluster == cluster_id, ]
  
  # Remove the 'cluster' column so that only gene expression data remain
  gene_data <- cluster_data[, setdiff(names(cluster_data), "cluster")]
  
  # Calculate the sum of expression for each gene (i.e., column sums over all cells in the cluster)
  gene_sums <- colSums(gene_data)
  
  # Sort the genes by summed expression in descending order and take the top 50 gene names
  top_50 <- names(sort(gene_sums, decreasing = TRUE)[1:50])
  
  return(top_50)
}

# Apply the function to each cluster (clusters 1 through 18)
top_50_per_cluster <- lapply(1:12, function(cluster_id) {
  get_top_50_per_cluster(mat_with_clusters, cluster_id)
})

  }
}

# Function to extract the top 50 gene names (columns) per cluster based on summed expression values
get_top_50_per_cluster <- function(mat_with_clusters, cluster_id) {
  # Subset rows (cells) belonging to the specified cluster
  cluster_data <- mat_with_clusters[mat_with_clusters$cluster == cluster_id, ]
  
  # Remove the 'cluster' column so that only gene expression data remain
  gene_data <- cluster_data[, setdiff(names(cluster_data), "cluster")]
  
  # Calculate the sum of expression for each gene (i.e., column sums over all cells in the cluster)
  gene_sums <- colSums(gene_data)
  
  # Sort the genes by summed expression in descending order and take the top 50 gene names
  top_50 <- names(sort(gene_sums, decreasing = TRUE)[1:50])
  
  return(top_50)
}
```
